back2basics.text: An Export Promotion Mission is a government initiative designed to enhance a country's export competitiveness by providing financial and non-financial support to exporters. It typically includes interventions to improve market access, compliance with international standards, and logistics infrastructure, especially targeting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Such missions help exporters overcome barriers to international trade and expand into new markets.

2026-11-19-am-0a388397d0.deck: On 17 November 2026, the Department of Commerce amended guidelines under four interventions of the Export Promotion Mission to enhance support for MSME exporters. These changes aim to improve market access, compliance assistance, and logistics support, especially for exporters in low export-intensity areas.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the recent amendments under the Export Promotion Mission:
1. The maximum eligible export turnover for airfare reimbursement under Market Access Support was increased from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore.

mcq.trap: A common trap is to confuse the previous turnover limit (₹75 lakh) with the new limit (₹50 crore) or to overlook the extension of air freight support to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh under LIFT.

body.label: Market Access Support (MAS)
body.text: The maximum eligible export turnover for airfare reimbursement increased from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore, with airfare reimbursement raised to 95% for micro and small exporters and 80% for others; the mandatory Export Promotion Council membership period was reduced from six to three months.

body.label: Trade Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement (TRACE)
body.text: The list of certificates eligible for reimbursement expanded from 462 to 600, helping MSMEs meet international quality, safety, and technical standards.

body.label: Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT)
body.text: Coverage of low export-intensity districts expanded from 13 to 34 States/UTs; eligible ports now include Land Customs Stations and Integrated Check Posts; waterways added as a transport mode; air freight support extended to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh; minimum distance criterion reduced from 200 km to 100 km; support extended to all exportable merchandise except those in a negative list.

body.label: Addressing logistical challenges

back2basics.text: The electoral roll is an official list of eligible voters maintained by the Election Commission. Voter enumeration is the process of registering voters and updating the roll to reflect changes such as deaths, shifts, or duplicates. Forms like Form 6 are used for new voter registration, while Form 7 is used for corrections or deletions. Accurate rolls ensure fair elections by preventing fraud and disenfranchisement.

2026-11-19-am-2aca9fe25d.deck: A public interest litigation in the Supreme Court seeks disclosure of how many voters removed under absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories have refilled enumeration forms to re-enter electoral rolls. This issue highlights concerns about electoral roll accuracy and voter rights, relevant for electoral reforms and democratic processes.

body.label: ASDD voter removal
body.text: Voters marked as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate (ASDD) were deleted from draft electoral rolls during a Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

body.label: Submission of enumeration forms
body.text: Some ASDD voters submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the rolls, but the exact number is unknown and sought by petitioners.

body.label: Form 6 misuse
body.text: Form 6, meant for new voter registration, was used by excluded voters to re-enter rolls, which the Supreme Court called an 'error' since it requires applicants to declare they are first-time voters.

body.label: Election Commission directive
body.text: The Election Commission allowed ASDD voters in seven states, including Delhi, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6.

body.label: Concerns over Form 7 misuse
body.text: The petition also raised concerns about misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions and requested an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications.

body.label: Transparency in political party role
body.text: It was requested that booth-level agents filing Form 7 identify themselves as party representatives rather than individuals.

body.text: Ensuring voters removed under ASDD categories can restore their names protects their right to vote and prevents disenfranchisement.

body.label: Transparency and accountability

back2basics.text: The Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme is a government initiative that allows investors to buy bonds denominated in grams of gold instead of physical gold. These bonds pay interest and can be redeemed at maturity or prematurely after a specified period. The scheme reduces the risks and costs associated with holding physical gold and helps the government mobilize resources.

back2basics.concept: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)
back2basics.text: CBDR-RC is a principle under international environmental law recognizing that while all countries are responsible for addressing global environmental destruction, they have different capabilities and differing responsibilities based on their historical contributions to the problem. It underpins climate negotiations by emphasizing equity and fairness in climate action commitments.

mcq.trap: Statement 1 is correct about the tariff reduction under the trade agreement; statement 2 is correct about the increased duty due to customs classification, so both statements are true.

body.label: Trade agreement background
body.text: The India-UK trade agreement implemented in July 2026 halved tariffs on Scotch whisky to 75%, which was seen as a win for companies importing Scotch in bulk.

body.label: Customs classification dispute
body.text: Indian investigators argued that bulk Scotch concentrates were misclassified under customs as raw materials, leading to reclassification under a new category attracting a 150% tariff plus consumption tax, totaling 162.5%.

body.label: Impact on imports
body.text: More than 80 containers of bulk Scotch from Pernod Ricard, Diageo, and Bacardi remain stuck at Indian ports due to this dispute.

sections.heading: What triggered the increase in duty on bulk Scotch imports?

body.label: Economic stakes
body.text: India is the largest market for Scotch by volume, with about 80% of Scotch imports arriving in bulk to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL).

body.label: Industry concerns
body.text: Companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo argue both bulk and bottled Scotch should be taxed at 75% under the trade agreement, fearing disruption and higher costs.

body.label: Diplomatic efforts
body.text: The British government is working with India to resolve the dispute, but the issue has already affected share prices and business continuity.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for India-UK trade relations and the liquor industry?

body.label: New customs category
body.text: Since May 2026, bulk Scotch concentrates are classified under 'compound alcoholic preparations' attracting a 150% tariff.

body.label: Additional taxes
body.text: Besides the tariff, a consumption tax is applied, raising the total duty to 162.5%.

body.label: Enforcement and challenges
body.text: Importers must pay 75% of the goods' value upfront with bank guarantees for the rest, creating working capital stress especially for smaller companies.

back2basics.concept: Right to Information Act and exemptions
back2basics.text: The Right to Information Act allows citizens to access government information to promote transparency and accountability. However, it also provides exemptions to protect sensitive information related to security, investigations, and privacy to prevent misuse or harm. Balancing transparency with confidentiality is essential for effective governance and law enforcement.

2026-11-19-am-a7119a51a1.deck: The Kerala High Court was informed by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) that T1 and T2 sections contain sensitive information requiring protection from Right to Information (RTI) disclosure. body.label: T2 Section contents
body.text: The T2 Section handles source reports, intelligence inputs, orders for surprise checks, confidential verifications, petitions, inquiries, and sensitive transferred cases.

body.label: T1 Section contents
body.text: The T1 Section deals with similar sensitive matters plus annual confidential reports (ACRs) of bureau staff and personal files of executive staff.

body.label: Nature of sensitivity
body.text: Disclosing intelligence inputs could alert public servants under investigation, allowing them to conceal evidence and intimidate informants.

sections.heading: What are the T1 and T2 sections and why are they sensitive?

body.label: Protection of investigations
body.text: The VACB argued that revealing intelligence or inquiries would compromise investigations and expose informants to retaliation.

body.label: Functions of VACB
body.text: VACB conducts surprise checks, surveils officers with doubtful integrity, maintains dossiers on corrupt officials, collects intelligence, and lays traps.

body.label: Processing of petitions
body.text: Only petitions requiring confidential verification or surprise checks are transferred to T1 or T2 sections; others are handled separately.

sections.heading: How does the VACB justify exemption from RTI?

body.label: Reassignment of certain functions
body.text: Functions related to ACRs of ministerial, executive, and legal staff and personal files were moved to the establishment section, which remains under RTI.

body.label: No blanket exclusion
body.text: The affidavit clarified that the GO did not exclude the entire VACB from RTI, only sensitive intelligence and inquiry data.

body.label: Session overview
body.text: The session provided a platform to share India's government initiatives to strengthen inclusive education and ensure equitable access for children with special needs (CwSN).

body.label: Implementation of CRPD
body.text: The Department highlighted key interventions under Samagra Shiksha aimed at inclusive education through a life-cycle approach covering early identification, individualized support, accessibility, therapeutic interventions, skilling, and exam-related facilities by CBSE.

body.label: PRASHAST tool
body.text: PRASHAST, a disability screening checklist for early identification of 21 disabilities among children aged 3 to 18, was discussed, including its revamped 2.0 mobile app integrated with UDISE+ that reduced screening time from three days to 15 minutes.

body.label: Field visit

back2basics.text: Industrial policy involves government measures to promote industrial growth and development. Such clusters attract investment, create jobs, and help build domestic capabilities.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior:
1. The Central Government is funding Phase-I of the project with ₹493 crore.
2. The Government of Madhya Pradesh holds 49% equity in the Special Purpose Vehicle established for the project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the Government of Madhya Pradesh holds 51% equity, not 49%, in the Special Purpose Vehicle; the Department of Telecommunications holds 49%.

body.label: Asia’s first integrated cluster
body.text: The zone is envisioned as Asia’s first integrated telecom manufacturing cluster, providing an ecosystem for manufacturing, R&D, innovation, and technology partnerships in mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment, and 5G/6G technologies.

body.label: Land and funding support
body.text: The Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost, while the Central Government is funding Phase-I with ₹493 crore.

body.label: Special Purpose Vehicle
body.text: A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been created for the project development, with 51% equity from Madhya Pradesh and 49% from the Department of Telecommunications.

sections.heading: What is the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior?

body.label: Strengthening domestic manufacturing
body.text: The zone aims to strengthen India’s domestic telecom manufacturing capabilities and reduce import dependence.

body.label: Promoting innovation and technology
body.text: It will foster research, development, and innovation in next-generation telecom technologies like 5G and 6G.

body.label: Economic and employment impact
body.text: The initiative is expected to boost Madhya Pradesh’s industrial ecosystem, encourage investment, promote technology-driven entrepreneurship, and create skilled employment opportunities.

body.label: Alignment with Aatmanirbhar Bharat
body.text: The project supports the government’s vision of self-reliance by promoting indigenous design, manufacturing, and positioning India as a global telecom hub.

sections.heading: Why does the Telecom Manufacturing Zone matter?

body.label: Stakeholder involvement
body.text: Representatives from the telecom industry and industry associations participated, sharing perspectives on investment and industry participation.

body.label: Government presentations
body.text: The Government of Madhya Pradesh presented the project roadmap, followed by addresses on the Government of India's telecom manufacturing vision.
